## Version 7.17.2 — 2026-11-04

- Fix: two different scenarios failed with “attempt to write a readonly database”. These were regressions in 7.17.1. They are fixed, closing [issue 2356](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2356):
  - When using a version of SQLite older than 3.34.0, such as on RHEL 8 or Ubuntu 20.04, `coverage combine` (and pytest-cov, which combines automatically) always failed.
  - `coverage combine` and `coverage debug data` failed when a data file existed but had no coverage schema, for example an empty file left behind by a worker that died. A file we can’t read is now reported like any other unusable data file, and is left in place.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.17.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.17.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.17.2`

## Version 7.17.1 — 2026-11-03

- Fix: a one-line class or function body immediately followed by another statement (such as `class Foo: ...` on its own line) was incorrectly reported as a missing branch when using the sys.monitoring core. This is now fixed, closing [issue 2167](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2167) and [issue 2337](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2337).
- Fix: the HTML report only rewrites a file’s page when the file or its data has changed, but each page also links to the previous and next files. When the set of reported files changed, unchanged pages kept their old links. For example, with `skip_covered`, a file that became 100% covered had its page deleted, but the pages next to it still linked to it. Now a page is also rewritten when its neighbors change.
- Fix: `--fail-under` now uses at least the decimal precision of the threshold for both the comparison and failure message. With `precision=0`, a total of 0.4 now passes `--fail-under=0.3` and fails `--fail-under=0.5` with the message “total of 0.4 is less than fail-under=0.5”. Previously, the comparison rounded the total to zero and the message could claim “1 is less than 0”. Closes [issue 2295](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2295).
- Fix: the HTML report escaped file names twice, so a name with `&`, `<`, or quotes in it was shown with entities like `&`. Now they are properly escaped only once.
- Fix: `--source=/` measured no files. A file system root can’t be a source directory, so now it is an error. Closes [issue 2291](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2291).
- In an abundance of caution, prevent forged SQLite journal files from deleting files they shouldn’t.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.17.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.17.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.17.1`

## Version 7.17.0 — 2026-10-22

- Dropped support for Python 3.10.
- Binary wheels are now provided for iOS and Android. This allows the use of the optimized C tracer on mobile platforms.
- Fix: three or more levels of nested `with` statements could make a `with` line look like a branch with an exit that can never happen. Using the sys.monitoring core, these phantom branches were reported as partial. Other cores hid the problem but still counted the phantom branches in the total. Closes [issue 1987](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1987).
- Fix: a comment or string that merely mentioned `if True:` or `while True:` could mark its line as a branch that is known to be partial, so a branch that never ran was reported as taken. These built-in patterns now only match at the start of the statement. Closes [issue 2314](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2314).
- Fix: region detection missed functions defined in unusual places, such as `else` and `except` clauses. This is now fixed.
- Fix: recent versions of the lcov tool complain if the same function name appears more than once in a report. Python can have multiple same-named functions in a few ways, for example, getters/setters or conditionally defined functions. These are now disambiguated by adding a `@<line number>` suffix to the function name. Fixes *issue 2335*.
- Fix: The “Can’t combine statement coverage data with branch data” error now names the two data files it couldn’t combine. The [error description](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/messages.html#error-cant-combine) in the docs now lists common causes and how to find the process that wrote the file.
- Fix: at coverage totals close to 0 or 100, the XML report could get incorrect `line-rate` values like `8.333e-05` or `1`. This is now fixed, closing [issue 2293](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2293) and [issue 2294](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2294).
- Fix: a parallel data file saved more than once kept the hash of its first save in its file name. Combining could then skip it as a duplicate of another file that had the same data at that point, and delete it, losing the data recorded after the first save. Each save now updates the hash. This had been a problem since 7.13.1. Fixes [issue 2338](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2338).
- Fixes for obscure but legal file names:
  - File names (and plugin names) can contain control characters, which are legal in POSIX paths but unsafe in reports: in XML 1.0 they make the document non-well-formed, and in a terminal they act as escape sequences (colors, title/clipboard sequences, cursor moves that forge output). Now the XML report, the text and Markdown summary reports, and `coverage debug data` replace non-printable characters in names. Printable names are unchanged.
  - A file pattern (from `include`, `omit`, or a `[paths]` alias) containing a newline sent the glob-to-regex translation into an infinite loop, hanging the process. Newlines in patterns are now handled like any other character.
- Fixes in the implementation of the C tracer:
  - If a plugin’s `dynamic_source_filename` method raised an exception, lines in that function could be recorded as belonging to a different file. Also fixed some minor memory leaks in the C tracer.
  - The refcount of `None` was mismanaged during function calls, including comprehensions. This was unlikely to cause an actual problem, but is now fixed. Thanks, Andrew Dalke.
  - The C tracer held borrowed references to dictionary values, which was unsafe on free-threaded Python. Now it takes its own references.
  - An internal error while recording a new file could be reported as a confusing `SystemError` instead of the actual exception.
- Performance: the text summary report (`coverage report`) held on to every file’s parsed source until it finished, so its memory use grew with the size of the project: ten times or more what 7.14 used on large projects. Now it keeps only what it needs to print. Fixes [issue 2277](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2277).
- Performance: HTML reports should be about 5% faster to produce.
- Kept the political banner in the README. Closes [issue 2344](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2344).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.17.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.17.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.17.0`

## Version 7.16.2 — 2026-09-27

- Fix: on Python 3.14 and later, a `for` loop completing immediately before a function return could mistakenly report an uncovered branch. This is now fixed, closing [issue 2168](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2168).
- Fix: on Python 3.14 and later, the `else` clause of a `try` whose body is a `with` statement could incorrectly be reported as covered when the `with` raised. This is now fixed, closing [issue 2289](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2289).
- Fix: with `dynamic_context = test_function`, test methods written as `@staticmethod` or `@classmethod` were not given a context of their own. Now they are, on Python 3.11 and later. Closes [issue 1923](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1923).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.16.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.16.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.16.2`

## Version 7.16.1 — 2026-09-13

- Fix: when the body of an irrefutable `case` (like `case _:`) is entirely excluded, the `case` line is now excluded too, just as an excluded `else:` body removes the `else:` line. Previously the `case` line was left behind and reported as missing. Closes [issue 1563](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1563) with [pull 2269](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2269).
- Fix: using [CoverageData.update()](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coveragedata.html#coverage.CoverageData.update) twice on an in-memory database would fail, as described in [issue 2279](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2279). This is now fixed.
- Fix: the Total row in the footer of the HTML report’s index page was recomputed in JavaScript with rounding that could disagree with the total the server rendered in the heading, including showing `100%` when coverage was not complete. The footer now clamps values the way the rest of the report does, and when nothing is filtered out it is shown exactly as the server rendered it, so the two can’t disagree. That also keeps rows the report omits (`--skip-covered` drops fully covered files) in the total. Fixes [issue 2256](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2256).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.16.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.16.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.16.1`

## Version 7.16.0 — 2026-08-28

- When combining files, now path separator slashes will automatically be converted to the local file system style. This makes it less necessary to define `[paths]` configuration to combine data across operating systems. Fixes [issue 2266](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2266).
- The [Coverage.switch\_context()](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html#coverage.Coverage.switch_context) method now returns the previous context.
- Fix: previously, a `[paths]` pattern would be replaced everywhere in a file path when it was only meant to be replaced once, in the leading portion of the path. This is now fixed, in [pull 2268](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2268).
- Fixes to validation of options and configuration settings:
  - Negative precision settings now always cause useful error messages ([pull 2261](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2261)).
  - An invalid regex in the `--contexts` option (or the `[report] contexts` setting) reported a confusing “Couldn’t use data file …: user-defined function raised exception” error. Now it raises a proper configuration error naming the bad regex, like other regex settings do ([pull 2262](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2262)).
  - Non-string values in TOML configuration settings now produce a helpful error message instead of a traceback. This affects list settings whose elements aren’t strings (like `omit`, `exclude_lines`, or a `[paths]` entry), file settings like `data_file`, and any wrong-typed value in the `[paths]` section ([pull 2263](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2263)).
  - `coverage run` refuses run-affecting command-line options like `--branch` alongside `--concurrency=multiprocessing`, since they can’t reach the subprocesses. The check only recognized `multiprocessing` as the entire option value, so `--concurrency=multiprocessing,thread` slipped through and failed later with “Can’t combine statement coverage data with branch data”. Each named concurrency library is now properly considered ([pull 2270](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2270)).
- Fix: `coverage annotate -d DIR` raised an `AssertionError` if any measured file had an extension other than `.py`, such as a `.pyw` file on Windows. The original extension is now restored on the annotated copy ([pull 2265](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2265)).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.16.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.16.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.16.0`

## Version 7.15.4 — 2026-08-06

- Fix: in the HTML report, a source file name containing a double quote (legal on POSIX) wasn’t escaped where it’s dropped into the `href` of the index and prev/next links, so it could close the attribute early and inject markup. Page URLs are now escaped. Thanks, [Rajath Mohare](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2227).
- Fix: the LCOV report wrote file names and other fields into its line-oriented records without neutralizing control characters. A measured file whose name contained a newline (legal on POSIX) could forge extra records, inflating the coverage seen by tools that read the report. Control characters in a field are now replaced. Thanks, [Rajath Mohare](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2226).
- Wheels are now provided for Python 3.15.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.15.4](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.15.4).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.15.4`

## Version 7.15.3 — 2026-08-02

- Fix: the sysmon core is incompatible with dynamic contexts. Previously, the combination would be prevented when read from the coverage.py configuration. But using the context API as pytest-cov does, contexts would be silently dropped. Now a warning is issued, thanks to [Jisang Han](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2234). Closes [issue 2200](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2200).
- A performance improvement in the low-level line number bookkeeping when combining data files, thanks to [Kevin Turcios](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2239).
- Performance improvement in HTML reporting by reducing the number of times files have to be parsed, thanks to [Kevin Turcios](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2240).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.15.3](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.15.3).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.15.3`

## Version 7.15.2 — 2026-07-15

- Fix: one of the performance improvements in 7.15.1 (pull 2215) dramatically increased memory use during reporting for large projects. Now we use a different approach that is both faster and slimmer than 7.15.0. Fixes [issue 2229](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2229).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.15.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.15.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.15.2`

## Version 7.15.1 — 2026-07-12

- Fix: in the HTML report with `show_contexts` enabled, a context label containing `</script>` (for example a parametrized pytest node id) could close the inline `<script>` element in a file page early, injecting markup. Context labels are now fully escaped. Thanks, [Rajath Mohare](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2224).
- A number of performance improvements thanks to Paul Kehrer, in pull requests [2213](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2213), [2214](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2214), [2215](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2215), [2216](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2216), [2218](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2218), [2220](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2220), and [2221](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2221).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.15.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.15.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.15.1`

## Version 7.15.0 — 2026-07-02

- Since 7.14.0, reporting commands implicitly combine parallel data files. Now those commands have a new option `--keep-combined` to retain the data files after combining them instead of the default, which is to delete them. Finishes [issue 2198](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2198).
- Fix: the LCOV report would incorrectly count excluded functions as uncovered, as described in [issue 2205](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2205). This is now fixed thanks to [Martin Kuntz Jacobsen](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2206).
- When running your program, coverage now correctly sets `yourmodule.__spec__.loader` as [strongly recommended](), avoiding the deprecation warning described in [issue 2208](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2208). Thanks, [A5rocks](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2209).
- Fix: with Python 3.10, running with the `-I` (isolated mode) option didn’t correctly omit the current directory from the module search path, as described in [issue 2103](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2103). That is now fixed thanks to [Ilia Sorokin](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2211).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.15.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.15.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.15.0`

## Version 7.14.3 — 2026-06-22

- Fix: the default `...` exclusion rule now also matches function bodies whose closing return-type bracket is on its own line (for example, after a long `-> dict[ ... ]` annotation that a formatter has split over multiple lines). Closes [issue 2185](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2185), thanks [Mengjia Shang](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2196).
- Fix: On 3.13t, we incorrectly issued `Couldn't import C tracer` errors. We can’t import the C tracer because in 7.14.2 we stopped shipping compiled wheels for 3.13t. Thanks, [Hugo van Kemenade](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2203).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.14.3](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.14.3).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.14.3`

## Version 7.14.2 — 2026-06-20

- Fix: some messages were being written to stdout, making `coverage json -o -` useless for capturing JSON output. Now messages are written to stderr, fixing [issue 2197](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2197).
- Fix: `CoverageData` kept one SQLite connection per thread that recorded coverage, but never closed them when those threads terminated. On long runs with many short-lived threads this leaked one file descriptor per dead thread, eventually failing with `OSError: [Errno 24] Too many open files`. Connections belonging to terminated threads are now closed and dropped. Fixes [issue 2192](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2192). Thanks, [Matthew Lloyd](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2193).
- Fix: when using sys.monitoring, we were assuming we could use the `COVERAGE_ID` tool id. But other tools might also assume they could use that id. Pre-allocated ids don’t really make sense, so now we search for a usable one instead. Fixes [issue 2187](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2187).
- Following [the advice of cibuildwheel](https://py-free-threading.github.io/ci/#building-free-threaded-wheels-with-cibuildwheel), we no longer distribute wheels for Python 3.13 free-threaded.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.14.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.14.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.14.2`

## Version 7.14.1 — 2026-05-26

- Fix: the HTML report used typographic niceties to make file paths more readable by adding a small amount of space around slashes. Those spaces interfered with searching the page for file paths of interest. Now the report uses CSS to accomplish the same visual tweak so that searches with slashes work correctly. Closes [issue 2170](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2170).
- [Add a 3.16 PyPI classifier](https://mastodon.social/@hugovk/116588523571204490) since we test on the 3.16 main branch.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.14.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.14.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.14.1`

## Version 7.14.0 — 2026-05-10

- Feature: now when running one of the reporting commands, if there are parallel data files that need combining, they will be implicitly combined before creating the report. There is no option to avoid the combination; let us know if you have a use case that requires it. Thanks, [Tim Hatch](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2162). Closes [issue 1781](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1781).
- Fix: the output from `combine` was too verbose, listing each file considered. Now it shows a single line with the counts of files combined, files skipped, and files with errors. The `-q` flag suppresses this line. The old detailed lines are available with the new `--debug=combine` option.
- Fix: running a Python file through a symlink now sets the sys.path correctly, matching regular Python behavior. Fixes [issue 2157](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2157).
- Fix: `Collector.flush_data` could fail with “RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration” when a tracer in another thread added a line to the per-file set that `add_lines` (or `add_arcs`) was iterating. The values passed to `CoverageData` are now snapshotted via `dict.copy()` and `set.copy()`, which are atomic under the GIL. Thanks, [Alex Vandiver](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2165).
- Fix: the soft keyword `lazy` is now bolded in HTML reports.
- We are no longer testing eventlet support. Eventlet started issuing stern deprecation warnings that break our tests. Our support code is still there.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.14.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.14.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.14.0`

## Version 7.13.5 — 2026-03-17

- Fix: [issue 2138](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2138) describes a memory leak that happened when repeatedly using the Coverage API with in-memory data. This is now fixed.
- Fix: the markdown-formatted coverage report didn’t fully escape special characters in file paths ([issue 2141](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2141)). This would be very unlikely to cause a problem, but now it’s done properly, thanks to [Ellie Ayla](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2142).
- Fix: the C extension wouldn’t build on VS2019, but now it does ([issue 2145](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2145)).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.13.5](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.13.5).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.13.5`

## Version 7.13.4 — 2026-02-09

- Fix: the third-party code fix in 7.13.3 required examining the parent directories where coverage was run. In the unusual situation that one of the parent directories is unreadable, a PermissionError would occur, as described in [issue 2129](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2129). This is now fixed.
- Fix: in test suites that change sys.path, coverage.py could fail with “RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration” as described and fixed in [pull 2130](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2130). Thanks, Noah Fatsi.
- We now publish ppc64le wheels, thanks to [Pankhudi Jain](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2121).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.13.4](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.13.4).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.13.4`

## Version 7.13.3 — 2026-02-03

- Fix: in some situations, third-party code was measured when it shouldn’t have been, slowing down test execution. This happened with layered virtual environments such as uv sometimes makes. The problem is fixed, closing [issue 2082](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2082). Now any directory on sys.path that is inside a virtualenv is considered third-party code.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.13.3](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.13.3).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.13.3`

## Version 7.13.2 — 2026-01-25

- Fix: when Python is installed via symlinks, for example with Homebrew, the standard library files could be incorrectly included in coverage reports. This is now fixed, closing [issue 2115](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2115).
- Fix: if a data file is created with no read permissions, the combine step would fail completely. Now a warning is issued and the file is skipped. Closes [issue 2117](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2117).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.13.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.13.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.13.2`

## Version 7.13.1 — 2025-12-28

- Added: the JSON report now includes a `"start_line"` key for function and class regions, indicating the first line of the region in the source. Closes [issue 2110](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2110).
- Added: The `debug data` command now takes file names as arguments on the command line, so you can inspect specific data files without needing to set the `COVERAGE_FILE` environment variable.
- Fix: the JSON report used to report module docstrings as executed lines, which no other report did, as described in [issue 2105](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2105). This is now fixed, thanks to Jianrong Zhao.
- Fix: coverage.py uses a more disciplined approach to detecting where third-party code is installed, and avoids measuring it. This shouldn’t change any behavior. If you find that it does, please get in touch.
- Performance: data files that will be combined now record their hash as part of the file name. This lets us skip duplicate data more quickly, speeding the combining step.
- Docs: added a section explaining more about what is considered a missing branch and how it is reported: [Examples of missing branches](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/branch.html#branch-explain), as requested in [issue 1597](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1597). Thanks to [Ayisha Mohammed](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2092).
- Tests: the test suite misunderstood what core was being tested if `COVERAGE_CORE` wasn’t set on 3.14+. This is now fixed, closing [issue 2109](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2109).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.13.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.13.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.13.1`

## Version 7.13.0 — 2025-12-08

- Feature: coverage.py now supports `.coveragerc.toml` configuration files. These files use TOML syntax and take priority over `pyproject.toml` but lower priority than `.coveragerc` files. Closes [issue 1643](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1643) thanks to [Olena Yefymenko](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1952).
- Fix: we now include a permanent .pth file which is installed with the code, fixing [issue 2084](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2084). In 7.12.1b1 this was done incorrectly: it didn’t work when using the source wheel (`py3-none-any`). This is now fixed. Thanks, [Henry Schreiner](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2100).
- Deprecated: when coverage.py is installed, it creates three command entry points: `coverage`, `coverage3`, and `coverage-3.10` (if installed for Python 3.10). The second and third of these are not needed and will eventually be removed. They still work for now, but print a message about their deprecation.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.13.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.13.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.13.0`

name: 7.12.1b1
body:
## Version 7.12.1b1 — 2025-11-30

- Fix: coverage.py now includes a permanent .pth file in the distribution which is installed with the code. This fixes [issue 2084](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2084): failure to patch for subprocess measurement when site-packages is not writable.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.12.1b1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.12.1b1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.12.1b1`

## Version 7.12.0 — 2025-11-18

- The HTML report now shows separate coverage totals for statements and branches, as well as the usual combined coverage percentage. Thanks to Ryuta Otsuka for the [discussion](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2081) and the [implementation](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2085).
- The JSON report now includes separate coverage totals for statements and branches, thanks to [Ryuta Otsuka](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2090).
- Fix: `except*` clauses were not handled properly under the “sysmon” measurement core, causing KeyError exceptions as described in [issue 2086](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2086). This is now fixed.
- Fix: we now defend against aggressive mocking of `open()` that could cause errors inside coverage.py. An example of a failure is in [issue 2083](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2083).
- Fix: in unusual cases where a test suite intentionally exhausts the system’s file descriptors to test handling errors in `open()`, coverage.py would fail when trying to open source files, as described in [issue 2091](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2091). This is now fixed.
- A small tweak to the HTML report: file paths now use thin spaces around slashes to make them easier to read.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.12.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.12.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.12.0`

## Version 7.11.3 — 2025-11-09

- Fix: the 7.11.1 changes meant that conflicts between a requested measurement core and other settings would raise an error. This was a breaking change from previous behavior, as reported in [issue 2076](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2076) and [issue 2078](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2078).

  The previous behavior has been restored: when the requested core conflicts with other settings, another core is used instead, and a warning is issued.

- For contributors: the repo has moved from Ned’s [nedbat GitHub account](https://github.com/nedbat) to the [coveragepy GitHub organization](https://github.com/coveragepy). The default branch has changed from master to main.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.11.3](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.11.3).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.11.3`

## Version 7.11.2 — 2025-11-08

- Fix: using the “sysmon” measurement core in 7.11.1, if Python code was claimed to come from a non-Python file, a `NotPython` exception could be raised. This could happen for example with Jinja templates compiled to Python, as reported in [issue 2077](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2077). This is now fixed.
- Doc: corrected the first entry in the 7.11.1 changelog.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.11.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.11.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.11.2`

## Version 7.11.1 — 2025-11-07

- Fix: some chanages to details of how the measurement core is chosen, and how conflicting settings are handled. The “sysmon” core cannot be used with some concurrency settings, with dynamic context, and in Python 3.12/3.13, with branch measurement.
  - If the core is not specified and defaults to “sysmon” (Python 3.14+), but other settings conflict with sysmon, then the “ctrace” core will be used instead with no warning. For concurrency conflicts, this used to produce an error, as described in [issue 2064](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2064).
  - If the “sysmon” core is explicitly requested in your configuration, but other settings conflict, an error is now raised. This used to produce a warning.
- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the sys.monitoring core, as described in [issue 2070](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2070). This is now fixed.
- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a `breakpoint()` would stop in the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in [issue 1420](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1420). This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a slight performance improvement, but I couldn’t reproduce the performance gain, so it’s been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.
- A new debug option `--debug=core` shows which core is in use and why.
- Split `sqlite` debugging information out of the `sys` [coverage debug](commands/cmd_debug.rst#cmd-debug) and [--debug option](commands/cmd_debug.rst#cmd-run-debug) options since it’s bulky and not very useful.
- Updated the [How coverage.py works](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/howitworks.html#howitworks) page to better describe the three different measurement cores.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.11.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.11.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.11.1`

## Version 7.11.0 — 2025-10-15

- Dropped support for Python 3.9, declared support for Python 3.15 alpha.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.11.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.11.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.11.0`

## Version 7.10.7 — 2025-09-21

- Performance: with branch coverage in large files, generating HTML, JSON, or LCOV reports could take far too long due to some quadratic behavior when creating the function and class index pages. This is now fixed, closing [issue 2048](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2048). Thanks to Daniel Diniz for help diagnosing the problem.
- Most warnings and a few errors now have links to a page in the docs explaining the specific message. Closes [issue 1921](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1921).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.10.7](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.10.7).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.10.7`

## Version 7.10.6 — 2025-08-29

- Fix: `source` directories were not properly communicated to subprocesses that ran in different directories, as reported in [issue 1499](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1499). This is now fixed.
- Performance: [Alex Gaynor continues fine-tuning](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2038) the speed of combination, especially with many contexts.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.10.6](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.10.6).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.10.6`

## Version 7.10.5 — 2025-08-23

- Big speed improvements for `coverage combine`: it’s now about twice as fast! Huge thanks to Alex Gaynor for pull requests [2032](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2032), [2033](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2033), and [2034](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2034).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.10.5](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.10.5).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.10.5`

## Version 7.10.4 — 2025-08-16

- Added `patch = fork` for times when the built-in forking support is insufficient.
- Fix: `patch = execv` also inherits the entire coverage configuration now.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.10.4](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.10.4).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.10.4`

## Version 7.10.3 — 2025-08-10

- Fixes for `patch = subprocess`:
  - If subprocesses spawned yet more subprocesses simultaneously, some coverage could be missed. This is now fixed, closing [issue 2024](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2024).
  - If subprocesses were created in other directories, their data files were stranded there and not combined into the totals, as described in [issue 2025](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2025). This is now fixed.
  - On Windows (or maybe only some Windows?) the patch would fail with a `ModuleNotFound` error trying to import coverage. This is now fixed, closing [issue 2022](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2022).
  - Originally only options set in the coverage configuration file would apply to subprocesses. Options set on the `coverage run` command line (such as `--branch`) wouldn’t be communicated to the subprocesses. This could lead to combining failures, as described in [issue 2021](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2021). Now the entire configuration is used in subprocesses, regardless of its origin.
  - Added `debug=patch` to help diagnose problems.
- Fix: really close all SQLite databases, even in-memory ones. Closes [issue 2017](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2017).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.10.3](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.10.3).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.10.3`

## Version 7.10.2 — 2025-08-03

- Fix: some code with NOP bytecodes could report missing branches that are actually executed. This is now fixed, closing [issue 1999](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1999). Python 3.9 still shows the problem.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.10.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.10.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.10.2`

## Version 7.10.1 — 2025-07-27

- Fix: the exclusion for `if TYPE_CHECKING:` was wrong: it marked the branch as partial, but it should have been a line exclusion so the entire clause would be excluded. Improves [issue 831](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/831).
- Fix: changed where .pth files are written for `patch = subprocess`, closing [issue 2006](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2006).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.10.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.10.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.10.1`

## Version 7.10.0 — 2025-07-24

- A new configuration option: “[\[run\] patch](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#config-run-patch)” specifies named patches to work around some limitations in coverage measurement. These patches are available:
  - `patch = _exit` lets coverage save its data even when <https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os._exit> is used to abruptly end the process. This closes long-standing [issue 310](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/310) as well as its duplicates: [issue 312](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/312), [issue 1673](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1673), [issue 1845](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1845), and [issue 1941](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1941).
  - `patch = subprocess` measures coverage in Python subprocesses created with <https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#module-subprocess>, <https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.system>, or one of the <https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.execl> or <https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.spawnl> family of functions. Closes old [issue 367](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/367), its duplicate [issue 378](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/378) and old [issue 689](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/689).
  - `patch = execv` adjusts the <https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.html#os.execl> family of functions to save coverage data before ending the current program and starting the next. Not available on Windows. Closes [issue 43](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/43) after 15 years!
- The HTML report now dimly colors subsequent lines in multi-line statements. They used to have no color. This gives a better indication of the amount of code missing in the report. Closes [issue 1308](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1308).
- Two new exclusion patterns are part of the defaults: `...` is automatically excluded as a line and `if TYPE_CHECKING:` is excluded as a branch. Closes [issue 831](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/831).
- A new command-line option: `--save-signal=USR1` specifies a signal that coverage.py will listen for. When the signal is sent, the coverage data will be saved. This makes it possible to save data from within long-running processes. Thanks, [Arkady Gilinsky](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1998).
- A new configuration option: “[\[report\] partial\_also](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#config-report-partial-also)” is a list of regexes to add as pragmas for partial branches. This parallels the “[\[report\] exclude\_also](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#config-report-exclude-also)” setting for adding line exclusion patterns.
- A few file path configuration settings didn’t allow for tilde expansion: [\[json\] output](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#config-json-output), [\[lcov\] output](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#config-lcov-output) and [\[run\] debug\_file](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#config-run-debug-file). This is now fixed.
- Wheels are included for 3.14 now that 3.14 rc1 is available.
- We no longer ship a PyPy-specific wheel. PyPy will install the pure-Python wheel. Closes [issue 2001](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2001).
- In the very unusual situation of not having a current frame, coverage no longer crashes when using the sysmon core, fixing [issue 2005](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2005).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.10.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.10.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.10.0`

## Version 7.9.2 — 2025-07-03

- Fix: complex conditionals within a line might cause a KeyError when using sys.monitoring, as reported in [issue 1991](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1991). This is now fixed.
- Fix: we can now measure coverage for code in Python archive (.par) files. Thanks, [Itamer Oren](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1984).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.9.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.9.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.9.2`

## Version 7.9.1 — 2025-06-13

- The “no-ctracer” warning is not issued for Python pre-release versions. Coverage doesn’t ship compiled wheels for those versions, so this was far too noisy.
- On Python 3.14+, the “sysmon” core is now the default if it’s supported for your configuration. Plugins and dynamic contexts are still not supported with it.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.9.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.9.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.9.1`

## Version 7.9.0 — 2025-06-11

- Added a `[run] core` configuration setting to specify the measurement core, which was previously only available through the COVERAGE\_CORE environment variable. Finishes [issue 1746](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1746).
- Fixed incorrect rendering of f-strings with doubled braces, closing [issue 1980](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1980).
- If the C tracer core can’t be imported, a warning (“no-ctracer”) is issued with the reason.
- The C tracer core extension module now conforms to [PEP 489](https://peps.python.org/pep-0489), closing [issue 1977](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1977). Thanks, [Adam Turner](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1978).
- Fixed a “ValueError: min() arg is an empty sequence” error caused by strange empty modules, found by [oss-fuzz](https://google.github.io/oss-fuzz/).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.9.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.9.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.9.0`

## Version 7.8.2 — 2025-05-23

- Wheels are provided for Windows ARM64 on Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13. Thanks, [Finn Womack](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1972).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.8.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.8.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.8.2`

## Version 7.8.1 — 2025-05-21

- A number of EncodingWarnings were fixed that could appear if you’ve enabled PYTHONWARNDEFAULTENCODING, fixing [issue 1966](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1966). Thanks, [Henry Schreiner](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1967).
- Fixed a race condition when using sys.monitoring with free-threading Python, closing [issue 1970](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1970).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.8.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.8.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.8.1`

## Version 7.8.0 — 2025-03-30

- Added a new `source_dirs` setting for symmetry with the existing `source_pkgs` setting. It’s preferable to the existing `source` setting, because you’ll get a clear error when directories don’t exist. Fixes [issue 1942](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1942). Thanks, [Jeremy Fleischman](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1943).
- Fix: the PYTHONSAFEPATH environment variable new in Python 3.11 is properly supported, closing [issue 1696](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1696). Thanks, [Philipp A.](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1700). This works properly except for a detail when using the `coverage` command on Windows. There you can use `python -m coverage` instead if you need exact emulation.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.8.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.8.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.8.0`

## Version 7.7.1 — 2025-03-21

- A few small tweaks to the sys.monitoring support for Python 3.14. Please test!

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.7.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.7.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.7.1`

## Version 7.7.0 — 2025-03-16

- The Coverage object has a new method, [Coverage.branch\_stats()](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html#coverage.Coverage.branch_stats) for getting simple branch information for a module. Closes [issue 1888](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1888).
- The [Coverage constructor](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_coverage.html#coverage.Coverage) now has a `plugins` parameter for passing in plugin objects directly, thanks to [Alex Gaynor](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1919).
- Many constant tests in if statements are now recognized as being optimized away. For example, previously `if 13:` would have been considered a branch with one path not taken. Now it is understood as always true and no coverage is missing.
- The experimental sys.monitoring support now works for branch coverage if you are using Python 3.14.0 alpha 6 or newer. This should reduce the overhead coverage.py imposes on your test suite. Set the environment variable `COVERAGE_CORE=sysmon` to try it out.
- Confirmed support for PyPy 3.11. Thanks Michał Górny.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.7.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.7.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.7.0`

## Version 7.6.12 — 2025-02-11

- Fix: some aarch64 distributions were missing ([issue 1927](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1927)). These are now building reliably.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.6.12](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.6.12).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.6.12`

## Version 7.6.11 — 2025-02-08

- Fix: a memory leak in CTracer has been fixed. The details are in [issue 1924](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1924) and [pytest-dev 676](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/676). This should reduce the memory footprint for everyone even if it hadn’t caused a problem before.
- We now ship a py3-none-any.whl wheel file. Thanks, [Russell Keith-Magee](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1914).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.6.11](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.6.11).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.6.11`

## Version 7.6.10 — 2024-12-26

- Fix: some descriptions of missing branches in HTML and LCOV reports were incorrect when multi-line statements were involved ([issue 1874](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1874) and [issue 1875](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1875)). These are now fixed.
- Fix: Python 3.14 [defers evaluation of annotations](https://docs.python.org/3.14/whatsnew/3.14.html#whatsnew314-deferred-annotations) by moving them into separate code objects. That code is rarely executed, so coverage.py would mark them as missing, as reported in [issue 1908](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1908). Now they are ignored by coverage automatically.
- Fixed an obscure and mysterious problem on PyPy 3.10 seemingly involving mocks, imports, and trace functions: [issue 1902](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1902). To be honest, I don’t understand the problem or the solution, but `git bisect` helped find it, and now it’s fixed.
- Docs: re-wrote the [Managing processes](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subprocess.html#subprocess) page to put multiprocessing first and to highlight the correct use of <https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html#multiprocessing.pool.Pool>.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.6.10](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.6.10).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.6.10`

## Version 7.6.9 — 2024-12-06

- Fix: [Tomas Uribe fixed](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1901) a performance problem in the XML report. Large code bases should produce XML reports much faster now.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.6.9](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.6.9).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.6.9`

## Version 7.6.8 — 2024-11-23

- Fix: the LCOV report code assumed that a branch line that took no branches meant that the entire line was unexecuted. This isn’t true in a few cases: the line might always raise an exception, or might have been optimized away. Fixes [issue 1896](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1896).
- Fix: similarly, the HTML report will now explain that a line that jumps to none of its expected destinations must have always raised an exception. Previously, it would say something nonsensical like, “line 4 didn’t jump to line 5 because line 4 was never true, and it didn’t jump to line 7 because line 4 was always true.” This was also shown in [issue 1896](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1896).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.6.8](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.6.8).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.6.8`

## Version 7.6.7 — 2024-11-15

- Fix: ugh, the other assert from 7.6.5 can also be encountered in the wild, so it’s been restored to a conditional. Sorry for the churn.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.6.7](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.6.7).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.6.7`

## Version 7.6.6 — 2024-11-15

- One of the new asserts from 7.6.5 caused problems in real projects, as reported in [issue 1891](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1891). The assert has been removed.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.6.6](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.6.6).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.6.6`

## Version 7.6.5 — 2024-11-14

- Fix: fine-tuned the exact Python version (3.12.6) when exiting from `with` statements changed how they traced. This affected whether people saw the fix for [issue 1880](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1880).
- Fix: isolate our code more from mocking in the os module that in rare cases can cause [bizarre behavior](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov/issues/666).
- Refactor: some code unreachable code paths in parser.py were changed to asserts. If you encounter any of these, please let me know!

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.6.5](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.6.5).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.6.5`

## Version 7.6.4 — 2024-10-20

- Fix: multi-line `with` statements could cause contained branches to be incorrectly marked as missing ([issue 1880](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1880)). This is now fixed.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.6.4](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.6.4).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.6.4`

## Version 7.6.3 — 2024-10-13

- Fix: nested context managers could incorrectly be analyzed to flag a missing branch on the last context manager, as described in [issue 1876](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1876). This is now fixed.
- Fix: the missing branch message about not exiting a module had an extra “didn’t,” as described in [issue 1873](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1873). This is now fixed.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.6.3](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.6.3).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.6.3`

## Version 7.6.2 — 2024-10-09

- Dropped support for Python 3.8 and PyPy 3.8.

- Fix: On Python 3.7, a file with type annotations but no `from __future__ import annotations` would be missing statements in the coverage report. This is now fixed, closing [issue 1524](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1524).

## Version 7.0.4 — 2023-01-07

- Performance: an internal cache of file names was accidentally disabled, resulting in sometimes drastic reductions in performance. This is now fixed, closing [issue 1527](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1527). Thanks to Ivan Ciuvalschii for the reproducible test case.

## Version 7.0.3 — 2023-01-03

- Fix: when using pytest-cov or pytest-xdist, or perhaps both, the combining step could fail with `assert row is not None` using 7.0.2. This was due to a race condition that has always been possible and is still possible. In 7.0.1 and before, the error was silently swallowed by the combining code. Now it will produce a message “Couldn’t combine data file” and ignore the data file as it used to do before 7.0.2. Closes [issue 1522](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1522).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.0.3](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.0.3).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.0.3`

## Version 7.0.2 — 2023-01-02

- Fix: when using the `[run] relative_files = True` setting, a relative `[paths]` pattern was still being made absolute. This is now fixed, closing [issue 1519](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1519).
- Fix: if Python doesn’t provide tomllib, then TOML configuration files can only be read if coverage.py is installed with the `[toml]` extra. Coverage.py will raise an error if TOML support is not installed when it sees your settings are in a .toml file. But it didn’t understand that `[tools.coverage]` was a valid section header, so the error wasn’t reported if you used that header, and settings were silently ignored. This is now fixed, closing [issue 1516](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1516).
- Fix: adjusted how decorators are traced on PyPy 7.3.10, fixing [issue 1515](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1515).
- Fix: the `coverage lcov` report did not properly implement the `--fail-under=MIN` option. This has been fixed.
- Refactor: added many type annotations, including a number of refactorings. This should not affect outward behavior, but they were a bit invasive in some places, so keep your eyes peeled for oddities.
- Refactor: removed the vestigial and long untested support for Jython and IronPython.

## Version 7.0.1 — 2022-12-23

- When checking if a file mapping resolved to a file that exists, we weren’t considering files in .whl files. This is now fixed, closing [issue 1511](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1511).
- File pattern rules were too strict, forbidding plus signs and curly braces in directory and file names. This is now fixed, closing [issue 1513](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1513).
- Unusual Unicode or control characters in source files could prevent reporting. This is now fixed, closing [issue 1512](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1512).
- The PyPy wheel now installs on PyPy 3.7, 3.8, and 3.9, closing [issue 1510](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1510).

name: 7.0.0b1
body:
## Version 7.0.0b1 — 2022-12-03

A number of changes have been made to file path handling, including pattern matching and path remapping with the `[paths]` setting (see [\[paths\]](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#config-paths)). These changes might affect you, and require you to update your settings.

(This release includes the changes from [6.6.0b1](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/changes.html#changes-6-6-0b1), since 6.6.0 was never released.)

- Changes to file pattern matching, which might require updating your configuration:
  - Previously, `*` would incorrectly match directory separators, making precise matching difficult. This is now fixed, closing [issue 1407](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1407).
  - Now `**` matches any number of nested directories, including none.
- Improvements to combining data files when using the [\[run\] relative\_files](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#config-run-relative-files) setting, which might require updating your configuration:
  - During `coverage combine`, relative file paths are implicitly combined without needing a `[paths]` configuration setting. This also fixed [issue 991](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/991).
  - A `[paths]` setting like `*/foo` will now match `foo/bar.py` so that relative file paths can be combined more easily.
  - The [\[run\] relative\_files](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#config-run-relative-files) setting is properly interpreted in more places, fixing [issue 1280](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1280).
- When remapping file paths with `[paths]`, a path will be remapped only if the resulting path exists. The documentation has long said the prefix had to exist, but it was never enforced. This fixes [issue 608](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/608), improves [issue 649](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/649), and closes [issue 757](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/757).
- Reporting operations now implicitly use the `[paths]` setting to remap file paths within a single data file. Combining multiple files still requires the `coverage combine` step, but this simplifies some single-file situations. Closes [issue 1212](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1212) and [issue 713](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/713).
- The `coverage report` command now has a `--format=` option. The original style is now `--format=text`, and is the default.
  - Using `--format=markdown` will write the table in Markdown format, thanks to [Steve Oswald](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1479), closing [issue 1418](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1418).
  - Using `--format=total` will write a single total number to the output. This can be useful for making badges or writing status updates.
- Combining data files with `coverage combine` now hashes the data files to skip files that add no new information. This can reduce the time needed. Many details affect the speed-up, but for coverage.py’s own test suite, combining is about 40% faster. Closes [issue 1483](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1483).
- When searching for completely un-executed files, coverage.py uses the presence of `__init__.py` files to determine which directories have source that could have been imported. However, [implicit namespace packages](https://peps.python.org/pep-0420/) don’t require `__init__.py`. A new setting `[report] include_namespace_packages` tells coverage.py to consider these directories during reporting. Thanks to [Felix Horvat](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1387) for the contribution. Closes [issue 1383](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1383) and [issue 1024](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1024).
- Fixed environment variable expansion in pyproject.toml files. It was overly broad, causing errors outside of coverage.py settings, as described in [issue 1481](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1481) and [issue 1345](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1345). This is now fixed, but in rare cases will require changing your pyproject.toml to quote non-string values that use environment substitution.
- An empty file has a coverage total of 100%, but used to fail with `--fail-under`. This has been fixed, closing [issue 1470](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1470).
- The text report table no longer writes out two separator lines if there are no files listed in the table. One is plenty.
- Fixed a mis-measurement of a strange use of wildcard alternatives in match/case statements, closing [issue 1421](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1421).
- Fixed internal logic that prevented coverage.py from running on implementations other than CPython or PyPy ([issue 1474](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1474)).
- The deprecated `[run] note` setting has been completely removed.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 7.0.0b1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/7.0.0b1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==7.0.0b1`

name: 6.6.0b1
body:
## Version 6.6.0b1 — 2022-10-31

(Note: 6.6.0 final was never released. These changes are part of [7.0.0b1](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/changes.html#changes-7-0-0b1).)

- Changes to file pattern matching, which might require updating your configuration:
  - Previously, `*` would incorrectly match directory separators, making precise matching difficult. This is now fixed, closing [issue 1407](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1407).
  - Now `**` matches any number of nested directories, including none.
- Improvements to combining data files when using the [\[run\] relative\_files](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#config-run-relative-files) setting:
  - During `coverage combine`, relative file paths are implicitly combined without needing a `[paths]` configuration setting. This also fixed [issue 991](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/991).
  - A `[paths]` setting like `*/foo` will now match `foo/bar.py` so that relative file paths can be combined more easily.
  - The setting is properly interpreted in more places, fixing [issue 1280](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1280).
- Fixed environment variable expansion in pyproject.toml files. It was overly broad, causing errors outside of coverage.py settings, as described in [issue 1481](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1481) and [issue 1345](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1345). This is now fixed, but in rare cases will require changing your pyproject.toml to quote non-string values that use environment substitution.
- Fixed internal logic that prevented coverage.py from running on implementations other than CPython or PyPy ([issue 1474](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1474)).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.6.0b1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.6.0b1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.6.0b1`

## Version 6.5.0 — 2022-09-29

- The JSON report now includes details of which branches were taken, and which are missing for each file. Thanks, [Christoph Blessing](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1438). Closes [issue 1425](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1425).
- Starting with coverage.py 6.2, `class` statements were marked as a branch. This wasn’t right, and has been reverted, fixing [issue 1449](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1449). Note this will very slightly reduce your coverage total if you are measuring branch coverage.
- Packaging is now compliant with [PEP 517](https://peps.python.org/pep-0517/), closing [issue 1395](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1395).
- A new debug option `--debug=pathmap` shows details of the remapping of paths that happens during combine due to the `[paths]` setting.
- Fix an internal problem with caching of invalid Python parsing. Found by OSS-Fuzz, fixing their [bug 50381](https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=50381).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.5.0](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.5.0).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.5.0`

## Version 6.4.4 — 2022-08-16

- Wheels are now provided for Python 3.11.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.4.4](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.4.4).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.4.4`

## Version 6.4.3 — 2022-08-06

- Fix a failure when combining data files if the file names contained glob-like patterns. Thanks, [Michael Krebs and Benjamin Schubert](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1405).
- Fix a messaging failure when combining Windows data files on a different drive than the current directory, closing [issue 1428](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1428). Thanks, [Lorenzo Micò](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1430).
- Fix path calculations when running in the root directory, as you might do in a Docker container. Thanks [Arthur Rio](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1403).
- Filtering in the HTML report wouldn’t work when reloading the index page. This is now fixed. Thanks, [Marc Legendre](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1413).
- Fix a problem with Cython code measurement, closing [issue 972](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/972). Thanks, [Matus Valo](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1347).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.4.3](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.4.3).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.4.3`

## Version 6.4.2 — 2022-07-12

- Updated for a small change in Python 3.11.0 beta 4: modules now start with a line with line number 0, which is ignored. This line cannot be executed, so coverage totals were thrown off. This line is now ignored by coverage.py, but this also means that truly empty modules (like `__init__.py`) have no lines in them, rather than one phantom line. Fixes [issue 1419](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1419).
- Internal debugging data added to sys.modules is now an actual module, to avoid confusing code that examines everything in sys.modules. Thanks, [Yilei Yang](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1399).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.4.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.4.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.4.2`

## Version 6.4.1 — 2022-06-02

- Greatly improved performance on PyPy, and other environments that need the pure Python trace function. Thanks, Carl Friedrich Bolz-Tereick ([pull 1381](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1381) and [pull 1388](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1388)). Slightly improved performance when using the C trace function, as most environments do. Closes [issue 1339](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1339).
- The conditions for using tomllib from the standard library have been made more precise, so that 3.11 alphas will continue to work. Closes [issue 1390](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1390).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.4.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.4.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.4.1`

## Version 6.4 — 2022-05-22

- A new setting, [\[run\] sigterm](https://coverage.readthedocs.io/en/latest/config.html#config-run-sigterm), controls whether a SIGTERM signal handler is used. In 6.3, the signal handler was always installed, to capture data at unusual process ends. Unfortunately, this introduced other problems (see [issue 1310](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1310)). Now the signal handler is only used if you opt-in by setting `[run] sigterm = true`.
- Small changes to the HTML report:
  - Added links to next and previous file, and more keyboard shortcuts: `[` and `]` for next file and previous file; `u` for up to the index; and `?` to open/close the help panel. Thanks, [J. M. F. Tsang](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1364).
  - The time stamp and version are displayed at the top of the report. Thanks, [Ammar Askar](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1354). Closes [issue 1351](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1351).
- A new debug option `debug=sqldata` adds more detail to `debug=sql`, logging all the data being written to the database.
- Previously, running `coverage report` (or any of the reporting commands) in an empty directory would create a .coverage data file. Now they do not, fixing [issue 1328](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1328).
- On Python 3.11, the `[toml]` extra no longer installs tomli, instead using tomllib from the standard library. Thanks [Shantanu](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1359).
- In-memory CoverageData objects now properly update(), closing [issue 1323](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1323).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.4](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.4).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.4`

## Version 6.3.3 — 2022-05-12

- Fix: Coverage.py now builds successfully on CPython 3.11 (3.11.0b1) again. Closes [issue 1367](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1367). Some results for generators may have changed.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.3.3](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.3.3).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.3.3`

## Version 6.3.2 — 2022-02-20

- Fix: adapt to pypy3.9’s decorator tracing behavior. It now traces function decorators like CPython 3.8: both the @-line and the def-line are traced. Fixes [issue 1326](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1326).
- Debug: added `pybehave` to the list of [coverage debug](commands/cmd_debug.rst#cmd-debug) and [--debug option](commands/cmd_debug.rst#cmd-run-debug) options.
- Fix: show an intelligible error message if `--concurrency=multiprocessing` is used without a configuration file. Closes [issue 1320](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1320).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.3.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.3.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.3.2`

## Version 6.3.1 — 2022-02-01

- Fix: deadlocks could occur when terminating processes. Some of these deadlocks (described in [issue 1310](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1310)) are now fixed.
- Fix: a signal handler was being set from multiple threads, causing an error: “ValueError: signal only works in main thread”. This is now fixed, closing [issue 1312](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1312).
- Fix: `--precision` on the command-line was being ignored while considering `--fail-under`. This is now fixed, thanks to [Marcelo Trylesinski](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1317).
- Fix: releases no longer provide 3.11.0-alpha wheels. Coverage.py uses CPython internal fields which are moving during the alpha phase. Fixes [issue 1316](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1316).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.3.1](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.3.1).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.3.1`

## Version 6.3 — 2022-01-25

- Feature: Added the `lcov` command to generate reports in LCOV format. Thanks, [Bradley Burns](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1289). Closes issues [587](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/587) and [626](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/626).
- Feature: the coverage data file can now be specified on the command line with the `--data-file` option in any command that reads or writes data. This is in addition to the existing `COVERAGE_FILE` environment variable. Closes [issue 624](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/624). Thanks, [Nikita Bloshchanevich](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1304).
- Feature: coverage measurement data will now be written when a SIGTERM signal is received by the process. This includes <https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html#multiprocessing.Process.terminate>, and other ways to terminate a process. Currently this is only on Linux and Mac; Windows is not supported. Fixes [issue 1307](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1307).
- Dropped support for Python 3.6, which reached end-of-life on 2021-12-23.
- Updated Python 3.11 support to 3.11.0a4, fixing [issue 1294](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1294).
- Fix: the coverage data file is now created in a more robust way, to avoid problems when multiple processes are trying to write data at once. Fixes issues [1303](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1303) and [883](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/883).
- Fix: a .gitignore file will only be written into the HTML report output directory if the directory is empty. This should prevent certain unfortunate accidents of writing the file where it is not wanted.
- Releases now have MacOS arm64 wheels for Apple Silicon, fixing [issue 1288](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1288).

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.3](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.3).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.3`

## Version 6.2 — 2021-11-26

- Feature: Now the `--concurrency` setting can have a list of values, so that threads and another lightweight threading package can be measured together, such as `--concurrency=gevent,thread`. Closes [issue 1012](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1012) and [issue 1082](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1082). This also means that `thread` must be explicitly specified in some cases that used to be implicit such as `--concurrency=multiprocessing`, which must be changed to `--concurrency=multiprocessing,thread`.
- Fix: A module specified as the `source` setting is imported during startup, before the user program imports it. This could cause problems if the rest of the program isn’t ready yet. For example, [issue 1203](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1203) describes a Django setting that is accessed before settings have been configured. Now the early import is wrapped in a try/except so errors then don’t stop execution.
- Fix: A colon in a decorator expression would cause an exclusion to end too early, preventing the exclusion of the decorated function. This is now fixed.
- Fix: The HTML report now will not overwrite a .gitignore file that already exists in the HTML output directory (follow-on for [issue 1244](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1244)).
- API: The exceptions raised by Coverage.py have been specialized, to provide finer-grained catching of exceptions by third-party code.
- API: Using `suffix=False` when constructing a Coverage object with multiprocessing wouldn’t suppress the data file suffix ([issue 989](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/989)). This is now fixed.
- Debug: The `coverage debug data` command will now sniff out combinable data files, and report on all of them.
- Debug: The `coverage debug` command used to accept a number of topics at a time, and show all of them, though this was never documented. This no longer works, to allow for command-line options in the future.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.2`

## Version 6.1.2 — 2021-11-10

- Python 3.11 is supported (tested with 3.11.0a2). One still-open issue has to do with [exits through with-statements](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1270).
- Fix: When remapping file paths through the `[paths]` setting while combining, the `[run] relative_files` setting was ignored, resulting in absolute paths for remapped file names ([issue 1147](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1147)). This is now fixed.
- Fix: Complex conditionals over excluded lines could have incorrectly reported a missing branch ([issue 1271](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1271)). This is now fixed.
- Fix: More exceptions are now handled when trying to parse source files for reporting. Problems that used to terminate coverage.py can now be handled with `[report] ignore_errors`. This helps with plugins failing to read files ([django\_coverage\_plugin issue 78](https://github.com/coveragepy/django_coverage_plugin/issues/78)).
- Fix: Removed another vestige of jQuery from the source tarball ([issue 840](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/840)).
- Fix: Added a default value for a new-to-6.x argument of an internal class. This unsupported class is being used by coveralls ([issue 1273](https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1273)). Although I’d rather not “fix” unsupported interfaces, it’s actually nicer with a default value.

:arrow_right:  PyPI page: [coverage 6.1.2](https://pypi.org/project/coverage/6.1.2).
:arrow_right:  To install: `python3 -m pip install coverage==6.1.2`
